# Mission: sweep of 16 poles

Colour in 16 random poles that have no record yet, about 2 minutes each. One branch, one pre-registration commit,
one batch run, one PR. No claims: a pole someone else also tests gets two independent results, which is good.

1. Branch: git checkout -b sweep/moridinamael-2026-10-18
2. Draw: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play draw --k 16   (prints 16 pole ids; note them)
3. For each pole: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play card --neuron <id>   (seconds, no GPU: top examples, density, flags)
   If it is unclear, try a few sentences: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play probe --neuron <id> "…" "…"
   Probing loads the model each call, so probe several poles' sentences in a scratch script if you need many.
   Label at the level the card supports: usually a token or a context. A pole the card flags dense or positional
   gets "unit_kind": "dense / positional" and a best-effort test; do not force a meaning.
4. Pre-register all of them: uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play new interpret --neuron <id1> <id2> … --handle moridinamael
   Fill every tests file: label, 8 fire sentences, 8 near misses (same topic and style, without the trigger),
   methods.agent (who you are) and methods.screens (e.g. look, card, probe). quick-8+8@2 judges each: AUROC >= 0.90,
   median fire >= 0.20 of the pole's max, at most 1 near miss >= 0.30.
   Commit ALL tests files together and ALONE: git add <the tests files> && git commit -m "Pre-register sweep tests"
5. Run them all at once (one model load): uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.play run <all the tests files>
   Commit the results SEPARATELY: git add graph/contributions && git commit -m "Sweep results: <held>/<total> held"
6. Validate (uv run python -m bonsai_interp.graph.validate), push, and open one PR:
   cp .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/interpret.md pr.md (fill it in; one line per pole: id, label, outcome), then
   git push -u origin sweep/moridinamael-2026-10-18 && gh pr create --repo moridinamael/bonsai-interp --title "sweep: 16 poles (<held> held)" --body-file pr.md  (then delete pr.md)
   The merge agent merges conforming PRs once the checks pass, and regenerates the map.

Failed labels are results too; record them and move on. Do not re-test inside a sweep: a second round is a new mission.

Rules (from AGENTS.md; once CI is enabled it enforces 1-3, and play run already refuses uncommitted tests):
1. Commit the .tests.json ON ITS OWN before running anything that scores it; results go in a SECOND commit. Never amend, squash or edit a committed .tests.json.
2. Never edit or delete files under graph/contributions/ (yours included). Do not commit graph/neurons, edges.json or index.json: the merge agent regenerates them on main after merging.
3. Only the two contribution files (<= 64 KB each) go in git; bulky material goes to the library (DATA_POLICY.md).
4. Report honestly: a failed label is a valid contribution. Do not rewrite a test after seeing its result.

When done, tell the person in two or three sentences what you found and give them the PR link.

**10 of 16 held.** PR: https://github.com/moridinamael/bonsai-interp/pull/5

The strongest results were clean word-level units: "bristle/bristly" (L4/N6462−), the "-able" ending in French and Spanish words like *raisonnable* and *razonable* (L3/N8018−), and "classic/seminal work" (L8/N11255−) each fired on 8/8 with no near misses firing. Topic-level labels also held: Development Goals, "free of charge" pricing, charge carriers, "sent out / go forth", and shopping-promotion text. The six that failed were the vague labels I gave to scattered cards: Python call arguments, "why shouldn't", CJK byte fragments, a split-off initial "t", and technical verbs. The French "essayer" label also failed, because 3 of its 8 near misses fired, so that pole probably responds to French verb text in general, not just "essayer".

Choices I made:
- I wrote every label from the card alone and probed nothing before pre-registering, to stay at the brief's "about 2 minutes each".
- At first I created three tests files on the opposite pole to the one drawn (L22/N7290, L3/N8018, L24/N10425). I deleted those before committing anything and re-made them on the drawn poles.
- I left your local `uv.lock` change alone; it is not in the PR.
- The commits are in order and not squashed: tests in `d2a6a6b`, results in `9a9d52e`. Validate reports 0 problems.

**Friction**
- `play card` prints "direct logit effect: weights unavailable: FileNotFoundError" on every card, even though doctor said READY. So the "tokens its output promotes" section that AGENTS.md promises never shows.
- The pass rule is hard to see from the output. "fire 2/8 → HELD" (L27) and "fire 3/8 → HELD" (L23) sit next to "fire 4/8 → FAILED" (L33). The judge uses AUROC and median, but the printed count reads like a pass/fail number.
- The brief suggests "card" as an entry for `methods.screens`, but "card" is not in the allowed list in the template, so I used "look".
- The PR template's checklist says to add "refreshed derived files from `fold`". AGENTS.md rule 3 and the brief both forbid committing those, so I rewrote that checklist line in the PR.
- The tests files are written with CRLF line endings on Windows, so git prints 16 CRLF→LF warnings at commit time.
- Nothing warns you if the poles you pass to `play new` differ from the ones `play draw` gave you. That is how my three pole mistakes slipped in.
- The tools were fast: each card took seconds, and all 16 tests ran in about 50 s on one model load.
